title: The double dual of a coherent module is coherent reflexive
statement: Let $X$ be an integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] and let $H$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Put $H^\vee=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(H,\mathcal O_X)$ and $H^{\vee\vee}=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(H^\vee,\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Then $H^{\vee\vee}$ is coherent and its evaluation morphism $H^{\vee\vee}\longrightarrow (H^{\vee\vee})^{\vee\vee}$ is an isomorphism. No normality of $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0AY4 (divisors-lemma-dual-reflexive), with the reflexive-hull observation immediately preceding divisors-remark-tensor.

proof.text: First $\mathcal O_X$ is coherent. On an affine chart $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module] with rank one gives $\mathcal O_W\cong\widetilde A$. Thus $\mathcal O_X$ is quasi-coherent in the affine-local definition [pqf-def-coherent]. It is of finite type because $1$ generates it. Since $X$ is locally Noetherian, [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] gives coherence.

For any coherent module $G$ on $X$, [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-hom-local-kernel] with target $\mathcal O_X$ expresses $G^\vee$ near each point as the kernel of a map between finite sums of restrictions of $\mathcal O_X$. These restrictions are coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-module-local-on-open-cover](1); their finite sums and the kernel are coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-modules-kernel-cokernel-sum](1),(3). By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-module-local-on-open-cover](2), $G^\vee$ is coherent globally. Apply this with $G=H$, then $G=H^\vee$. Write $Q=H^{\vee\vee}$; both $H^\vee$ and $Q$ are coherent. This establishes the coherence clause of the item.

source.place: Tag 01Y2 (coherent-lemma-tensor-hom-coherent), internal-Hom proof using Modules Tag 01CQ.

proof.text: Fix a nonempty affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $X$. The ring $A$ is a domain by [def-pc-integral-scheme] and is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. Put $P=H^\vee(W)$. Its restriction $H^\vee|_W$ is coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-module-local-on-open-cover](1), hence quasi-coherent and of finite type by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], so $P$ is a finite $A$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](a). The sheaf Hom definition [def-pur-sheaf-hom] identifies $Q(W)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_W}(H^\vee|_W,\mathcal O_W)$. The counit isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](3) identifies $H^\vee|_W$ with $\widetilde P$. Its adjunction (1) therefore gives an $A$-linear isomorphism $c:Q(W)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,A)$, taking a sheaf morphism $\varphi$ to its map $\varphi_W$ on sections: this is the stated adjunction formula, since the counit corresponds to the identity of $P$. Linearity follows because morphisms and scalar multiplication in sheaf Hom are sectionwise.

source.place: Tag 0AY4 (divisors-lemma-dual-reflexive), reduction to More on Algebra Tag 0AV3 on affine opens; Tag 0AY0 affine comparison.

proof.text: The $A$-module $A$ is finite and reflexive: every $A$-linear $f:A\to A$ is $a\mapsto af(1)$, so $A^*\cong A$ by $f\mapsto f(1)$, and under this identification the evaluation $A\to A^{**}$ is the identity. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-hom-reflexive-domain] with $R=A$, $M=P$ and $N=A$ to get that $B=\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,A)$ is reflexive. For the isomorphism $c:Q(W)\to B$ of step 3, evaluation satisfies $e_B\circ c=c^{**}\circ e_{Q(W)}$: both sides, on $q$ and $\lambda\in B^*$, equal $\lambda(c(q))$. Since $c$, $c^{**}$ and $e_B$ are isomorphisms, $e_{Q(W)}=(c^{**})^{-1}e_Bc$ is an isomorphism. For the empty affine open all section modules are zero, and their evaluation is the unique isomorphism of zero modules. Thus $Q(W)$ is reflexive for every affine open $W$.

source.place: Tag 0AV3 (more-algebra-lemma-dual-reflexive), applied with target A; reflexive-hull observation following definition-reflexive-hull.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-reflexive-module-comparison] to the coherent module $Q$ on the integral locally Noetherian scheme $X$. Step 4 gives condition (ii) on every affine open, so condition (i) gives that the actual sheaf evaluation $Q\to Q^{\vee\vee}$ is an isomorphism. With $Q=H^{\vee\vee}$ and its coherence from step 2, this proves both assertions. Every ring used in step 4 was a Noetherian domain; no normality hypothesis was used.
